split.note: both vendor files combined, then re-split with common.stratified_split (Spark sampleBy, so the split is approximately, not exactly, 80:20)

limitations: Labels are the dataset author's own judgement: one person hand-identified 'fake/spammer' accounts for a final-year project and states that a couple may be misidentified. 'Fake' and 'spammer' are merged by the author. Our 1 = Inauthentic is an operational convention, not proof of intent.
Collected by one crawler over 15-19 March 2019. Instagram, its users and fake-account tactics have changed since; nothing here shows the model would transfer to 2026 accounts.
Small: 696 accounts, test split n=107. One test account moves accuracy by 0.93 percentage points; see cross_validation and split_lottery for the spread.
Balanced 50/50 by construction. Real-world prevalence of fake accounts is unknown and certainly not 50%; precision in deployment would be lower than measured here.

Selection: accounts were chosen by the author, plausibly the clearer-cut cases. Borderline accounts (e.g. new genuine users with no picture and no posts) are likely under-represented - they are exactly the people a deployed model would wrongly flag.
Profile metadata only - no behaviour over time, no content, no network. Strongly predictive signals (no profile picture, digits in the username) are cheap for an adversary to change.
Both vendor files are sorted by class (all genuine rows first). Harmless for our shuffled splits, but any un-shuffled k-fold or head/tail split of these files would be badly biased.

dataset_info.name: Facebook Spam Dataset
dataset_info.positive_means: spam profile per the dataset author (mapped to 1 = Inauthentic)
dataset_info.collection_claimed_by_card: Facebook API / Graph API, public profiles; 500 legit + 100 spam

mapping.avg_tags: tags/post (card: 'average number of tags in a post / rate of tagging')
mapping.avg_hashtags: #tags/post (card: 'average number of hashtags present in a post')

limitations: Provenance is thin: the card claims Facebook (Graph) API collection from public profiles but gives no date, no sampling method and no labelling procedure, and the license is 'unknown'. The class counts in the file (497/103) do not match the card (500/100).
The values look partly constructed rather than measured (see leakage_audit.plausibility). Whatever the model learns here may describe how the file was made more than how spammers behave.

The file is two blocks (legit rows, then spam rows) and the features track the block more closely than the label (see leakage_audit.label_vs_file_block). The 23 rows whose label disagrees with their block are either mislabelled or deliberately mixed in; the model cannot tell, and neither can we.
'Spam' here is the author's label for a profile. It is not the same concept as Instagram 'fake' or X 'bot'; 1 = Inauthentic is an operational convention, not a claim about intent.
Small and imbalanced: 20 spam accounts in the test split, so one missed spam account moves recall by 5.0 percentage points.
Real-world spam prevalence is unknown; precision measured at 17% prevalence would fall at lower prevalence.
A near-perfect benchmark score must not be compared head-to-head with the harder platforms as if Facebook spam were easier to detect.

dataset_info.name: TikTok 2025 dataset (merged, deduplicated)
dataset_info.ground_truth: NONE. No label exists and none was created. Nothing in this file may be read as 'bot' or 'not bot'.

limitations: NO GROUND TRUTH. Every flag is an indicator for human review, never a bot label. The share of bots in this population is unknown, so the precision of any flag is unknown.
Bot does not mean harmful, and an indicator firing does not mean bot.
Popularity-filtered sample: every video has >= ~141k plays, and low-reach accounts are absent.
95.4% of authors have one video, so the strongest signal (timing) is undefined for them.
Posting intervals are between captured viral videos, not all uploads: they are thinned.
No follower / following / account-age / profile data: the features that matter on the labelled platforms do not exist here.
Counts are display-rounded (about 3 significant figures).
Engagement is not normalised for exposure time (scrape time unknown for 99.9% of rows).
Timestamp timezone is not documented. Values are treated as naive UTC, so hour-of-day features are not interpreted.
Coordination cannot be assessed (no links between accounts in the data).
views/plays and create_time/posted_time are assumed to be the same quantity under two names. This affects 7 rows and cannot be verified, because the columns never co-occur.

rules.priority_review: regular-posting fired, OR burst AND caption-duplication both fired
rules.secondary_context: exactly one of burst / caption-duplication fired
rules.weak_signal_only: only engagement-outlier and/or IsolationForest fired: do not queue on this alone
rules.no_indicator_fired: >= 1 behavioural indicator assessable and none fired (NOT 'authentic')
rules.behaviour_not_assessable: no behavioural indicator assessable (single-video authors) and no weak signal

review_tiers.why_not_a_score: The indicators differ in evidential weight and in who they can assess. Adding them up would let several weak, popularity-driven signals outrank one strong one, and would make a 5-indicator count look more precise than the data allows.

coordination_assessment.reason: The data has no follower / following graph, no reply or duet / stitch links, no shared device or network signal. Shared hashtags, sounds and captions are normal on TikTok (trends, platform programme tags), so they do not show that accounts are linked.

risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: Tidak menunjukkan indikasi kuat perilaku tidak autentik dari fitur yang tersedia.
risk_level_definitions.definition: Model score below t1 (or, TikTok: behaviour assessed and no behavioural indicator fired). NOT a statement that the account is authentic.
risk_level_definitions.required_evidence: an out-of-sample model score (or an assessable behavioural indicator)

risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: Ada indikasi otomatisasi atau pola aktivitas yang tidak biasa, tetapi bukti masih terbatas.
risk_level_definitions.definition: t1 <= score < t2. t1 maximises F2 (recall weighted 2x) on the calibration fold.
risk_level_definitions.required_evidence: an out-of-sample model score with measured precision/recall, from a model that passes the evidence gate
risk_level_definitions.suggested_action: monitor / sample for QA; review only if capacity allows

risk_level_definitions.name_id: Indikasi kuat tingkat akun - prioritas tinjauan manusia
risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: Indikasi perilaku tidak autentik atau spam lebih kuat.
risk_level_definitions.name_en: Strong account-level indication - priority human review
risk_level_definitions.definition: score >= t2. t2 maximises F0.5 (precision weighted 2x) on the calibration fold, because every flag spends a moderator's time and may put a real person in the queue.
risk_level_definitions.required_evidence: an out-of-sample model score whose precision at the cut has been measured against labels (impossible for TikTok)
risk_level_definitions.suggested_action: human review queue, ordered by score; never an automated sanction

risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: Ada indikasi pola koordinasi antar akun yang dapat didukung oleh data jaringan/waktu/konten.
risk_level_definitions.definition: Level 2 PLUS evidence that the account acts together with other accounts: synchronised posting times, shared or near-duplicate content across accounts, or shared infrastructure / network ties.
risk_level_definitions.required_evidence: per-post timestamps and content for many accounts in the same window, and/or an interaction or follow graph; platform-side device/IP signals
risk_level_definitions.suggested_action: escalate to an investigation analyst (still human)

risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: Indikasi koordinasi dan amplifikasi kuat serta mempunyai potensi impact yang lebih besar.
risk_level_definitions.definition: Level 3 PLUS evidence that the coordinated group amplifies a common target (cross-account bursts boosting the same post, URL or hashtag) with measurable reach.
risk_level_definitions.required_evidence: interaction event logs (who retweeted/shared/liked what, when), target identifiers, and reach over time
risk_level_definitions.suggested_action: escalate as a campaign investigation (still human)

risk_level_definitions.description_concept_doc: (tidak ada padanan di konsep §13; tier ditambahkan oleh track sintesis)
risk_level_definitions.definition: No evidence can be computed (TikTok single-video authors), or the model has no signal (evidence gate failed: X synthetic). Missing is not zero: this is NOT Level 0.
risk_level_definitions.suggested_action: none - and do not report as 'clear'
